text:
maria-cust: Hey team — we started seeing intermittent 429s this morning when we fan out requests across two model variants (rwd-large and rwd-medium). It only happens when the prompt + context is large (~96k chars, ~55k tokens) and we also prefetch embeddings in parallel. Any guidance on per-model RPM/TPM, max concurrency and how long-contexts affect throttling?

support-jess: Thanks — can you paste a minimal curl request and the exact response headers (X-Request-Id, X-RateLimit-*, and status body) if available? Also are you using one API key for all fanout requests or multiple keys?

maria-cust: Curl we used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"<huge-context>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Response snippet (one example):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_abc123
x-ratelimit-limit: 600
x-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset: 167
{ "error": { "message": "rate limit exceeded for model rwd-large" } }

We are definitely reusing a single key from our app. Also we see the 429 primarily when we fire the same flow across rwd-large + rwd-medium simultaneously (fanout).

support-jess: Got it. Two quick possibilities: per-model token-based throughput and concurrency floors. Long contexts consume many tokens on the input side so your effective TPM is much lower. Devon from runtime can add details, but can you tell us approximate call pattern (parallel requests per second, average response token length)?

maria-cust: Pattern: 35 parallel requests from a single app server, each fans out to 2 models -> ~70 concurrent model calls. Average final output ~400 tokens. Total input tokens per call ~55k.

devon-runtime: TL;DR: This is most likely hitting per-model TPM and concurrency constraints compounded by token accounting for long contexts. A few clarifications and notes: 
- Redwood enforces per-model RPM/TPM caps (token-based for some models). For very long contexts the token budget consumed per request is huge, so even a small RPS can exhaust TPM.
- Concurrency limits are per-instance and per-model family. rwd-large has lower max concurrency than rwd-medium on the same backend type.
- Fanout multiplies both RPM/TPM and concurrency usage (your 35 users -> 70 model calls).
- Prefetching embeddings in parallel also counts against throughput if you call the embeddings endpoint with the same key. 
- If X-RateLimit-Remaining is 0 and Reset is non-zero, that's a clear TPM/RPM hit. 429 vs queued requests: we sometimes return 429 instead of queuing when the model's variant pool is saturated to avoid head-of-line blocking.

samir-sre: Additional repro notes: when we repro locally with similar token counts we see token-processing latency spike and the scheduler starts rejecting new requests at the model router. Best practices to mitigate quickly: 
- Reduce fanout: try sequential model calls (large -> medium fallback) instead of parallel.
- Trim context: move old context to a vector DB and only supply a short retrieval window.
- Use smaller model variant for prefetch/embeds and reserve rwd-large for final generation.
- Add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (start 200ms -> double).

maria-cust: Any account-level knobs? We have enterprise plan but don't want to change code if we can avoid it right now.

billing-ryan: On enterprise tiers we can increase per-model reserved concurrency and raise TPM/RPM windows per contract. If you want us to temporarily bump values while you refactor, DM me your account ID and the exact timestamps of failures and we can open an escalation with provisioning. Note that quota bumps are temporary until a commit/contract change is made.

support-jess: For us to triage further, please provide: 1) a few full request IDs (x-request-id) from 429 responses, 2) the API key prefix (so we can correlate), and 3) whether you can test with sequential fanout. We'll also check server-side logs for queue rejections and per-model throttles.

maria-cust: Posting two sample request ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Key prefix: sk-prod-app1. We can try sequential fanout tomorrow morning.

devon-runtime: From the logs I pulled with those ids: we show per-model token consumption peaking and a concurrent_active count hitting rwd-large pool max (configured at 48 concurrent for your tier), which triggered fast-fail 429s for excess requests. rwd-medium still had spare capacity. So the immediate fix is to route prefetch/embeds to rwd-medium (or a smaller embed model) and reduce simultaneous calls to rwd-large. We can also enable a lightweight server-side per-request queue for a narrow window to smooth spikes — would need ops approval.

samir-sre: If you need a quick client-side mitigation: implement a semaphore limiting to ~40 parallel calls to the generation endpoint from that one API key (since 48 is pool max; leave headroom). Also make sure your retry does not aggressively reattempt all parallel requests at once.

oncall-bot: case #INC-2026-541 created and assigned to eng-runtime. ETA for first response 60m. :white_check_mark:

maria-cust: Thanks all — we'll throttle at 40 parallel, switch prefetch to rwd-medium, and report back with new request ids after testing. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:
